subject: Deal-triggered node reserve proposal (US/EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Kate Brooks <kate.brooks@cognia.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Tan <marcus.tan@cognia.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial capacity ask — Cognia deal forecasts attached

Hi Rishi,

Appreciate the quick connect today. As discussed, Cognia is targeting a phased rollout of our generative summarization feature across three regions. High-level ask: we expect steady-state demand of ~850 concurrent tokens/s in US, ~420 in EU, and an initial pilot in APAC that could spike to ~250 tokens/s during first 90 days.

We'd like to explore a deal-triggered node reservation that guarantees baseline QPS/latency for the first 6 months, with options to scale after milestone sign-offs. Attached is our traffic forecast for the next 12 months (Cognia_forecast_aug2027.csv).

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you outline a reservation mechanism that ties node reserves to deal milestones (e.g., contract execution, first production week, post-P0)?
- Which regions would you recommend reserving nodes in vs. meeting demand via burst/buffer pools?
- Typical lead times to pre-warm or pin nodes in EU and APAC?

We'd like a proposal by next Wednesday (9/6) so our procurement team can align on budget.

Thanks — looking forward,

Kate Brooks
Head of Platform Ops, Cognia Analytics
kate.brooks@cognia.ai
Attachment: Cognia_forecast_aug2027.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Brooks <kate.brooks@cognia.ai>
Cc: Marcus Tan <marcus.tan@cognia.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — Cognia deal forecasts attached

Hi Kate — thanks for the forecast, that helps. Putting a short proposal on what we can offer and some constraints. I've attached a working capacity model (capacity_model_v3.xlsx) we use to translate tokens/s into node equivalents and cost projection.

Preliminary thoughts (high level):
- US: recommend a reserved tranche sized to cover ~80% of steady-state (so reserve ~680 tokens/s equivalent). Use burst lanes for peak traffic.
- EU: reserve ~60% initially (~250 tokens/s eq.), pre-warm additional nodes as we hit month-over-month growth triggers.
- APAC: recommend on-demand for first 90 days with the option to convert to a small reserved pilot (2–4 nodes) if sustained.

Key proposal mechanics we prefer: deal-triggered reserve split across two milestones — 50% reserve on contract execution, remaining 50% on production sign-off. That keeps commitment aligned with go-live risk.

Open items I need from you:
- Confirmation of the expected 99th percentile latency SLO for user-facing calls (we assumed 250–300ms)
- Any geo restrictions (data residency) that require pure-private deployments in EU/APAC

If that works, I'll loop in Operations to check inventory across the target windows and get back with firm node counts and lead times.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Deal Engineering — Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_model_v3.xlsx

Subject: RE: Deal-triggered node reserve proposal (US/EU/APAC)

Folks — ran the numbers against current fleet. Below are three scenario options (rounded node counts; nodes=96GB A100 equiv). I kept assumptions in the workbook.

Scenario A — Conservative reserve:
- US: 8 reserved nodes (covers ~75–80% steady-state), burst available up to +3 nodes; lead time: 7–10 days for warm pools.
- EU: 4 reserved nodes; pre-warm +2 nodes on 2-week notice.
- APAC: 0 reserved, on-demand burst from shared pool.

Scenario B — Balanced (recommended for commercial SLA):
- US: 11 reserved nodes (covers baseline and small buffer), dedicated throughput lanes; lead time: 10 days.
- EU: 6 reserved nodes, +2 warm standby.
- APAC: pilot reserve of 2 nodes to curb cold-start tail latency.

Scenario C — Aggressive reserve (for peak-sensitive launches):
- US: 16 reserved nodes; EU: 10 reserved; APAC: 4 reserved.
- Higher cost but minimal burst reliance.

Ops notes: we have limited capacity for aggressive allocations across the 9/15–10/15 window due to other Q3 commitments. If Cognia needs Scenario B/C, we should secure tranche now and include a staggered ramp to avoid blocking in-flight deals.

I'll attach the annotated workbook with the assumptions.

—Laura
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Brooks <kate.brooks@cognia.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Deal-triggered node reserve proposal (US/EU/APAC)

Quick operational readout — inventory and procurement implications: 

- Current pool availability (week of 9/6): US shared pool has ~18 nodes free for reservation across our US sites; EU has 7 nodes free but several are earmarked for a pending onboarding; APAC is very tight (1–2 spare nodes).
- Lead-time to convert shared nodes to reserved (pin + dedicated routing): ~72 hours for US (if pre-warmed), ~5 business days for EU due to network and cert provisioning, ~10 business days for APAC (cloud partner window).
- SOW: we'll need a signed SOW that defines node hold time, overage billing, and failure fallback lanes. Draft SOW link: https://www.docusign.com/DEAL-5492/SOW-draft

Recommendation: approve a staged commitment — accept Scenario B with an initial US/EU tranche (11 US / 6 EU reserved) and a 2-node APAC pilot on demand to avoid blocking. We'll book a 14-day hold on the US nodes once Cognia signs LOI to guarantee visibility.

Ben Carter
Capacity Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW_draft_redwood.docx (referenced link)
From: Marcus Tan <marcus.tan@cognia.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal-triggered node reserve proposal (US/EU/APAC)

Thanks — that aligns with our internal risk tolerance. Cognia is prepared to move forward with the staged approach (Scenario B): 11 US / 6 EU reserved, APAC pilot on demand. We accept the milestone split you proposed (50% at contract execution, 50% at production sign-off), and we will route the SOW to procurement this afternoon.

Action items: 
- Redwood: please send a redlineable SOW and timeline for provisioning.
- Cognia: procurement will review and come back with any redlines by EOD Monday (9/6).

Appreciate the speed here — Kate and I will be on standby for any clarifications.

Best,
Marcus Tan
VP Product Ops, Cognia Analytics
